title: Repair a bracket checker
prompt: Return true when every bracket in text is closed by the right kind of bracket, in the right order. The brackets are ( ), [ ] and { }. Ignore every other character.
hints: Why does counting pass a text such as "(]"?
When a closing bracket arrives, it must match the most recent opening bracket that is still open. That is the top of a stack.
Push each opening bracket. On a closing bracket, pop and compare. Return false on a mismatch or an empty stack, and at the end return whether the stack is empty.
checkLabels: Nested brackets of three kinds are balanced.
A round bracket is not closed by a square one.
Brackets left open are not balanced.
A closing bracket with nothing to close is not balanced.
A text with no brackets is balanced.
Brackets must close in the reverse of the order they opened.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Counts brackets without checking that the kinds match.
Forgets to check that nothing is left open at the end.

feedback: A count cannot remember which kind of bracket is open. A stack can: its top is the bracket that must be closed next.
